newsitem.title: UK: LME metals recover, aluminium ends with small gain.
newsitem.headline: LME metals recover, aluminium ends with small gain.

text.p: LME metals recovered in the afternoon as a wave of trade buying gave the market a shot in the arm, traders said.
Three months aluminium finished the afternoon kerb in the positive column at $1,584, up $2 on the day, after earlier touching a low of $1,565.
In the morning commision house selling and disappointed liquidation triggered stops below $1,575 support, but trade buying came in at the lows, traders said.
Stocks fell by 4,350 tonnes, continuing a string of hefty inventory reductions.
"If stocks continue to fall like this and the shorts are still around, they will be forced out," said analyst William Adams of broker Rudolf Wolff.
The next significant support level was at $1,560 and then $1,540, chartists said.
Copper also dipped, moving down to $2,572, before finding support and finishing the day at $2,582, a loss of $6.
Prices nudged up to $2,602 in the morning, but the market has been overbought since scoring fresh highs last week at $2,609 and needs a pause, analysts said.
A flag was developing on the charts, indicating a break higher, Adams said.
The cash/threes backwardation ended slightly narrower at $88/$93.
Lead dropped to a 20-month low of $613 as more long liquidation battered prices before trade buying kicked in and sent them on a modest upswing to $622, up $1 on the day.
The market may consolidate around current levels, but was still vulnerable to further downside pressure. The next target on the downside would be around $600, traders said.
Physical traders say the market is deathly slow as consumers wittle down their stocks and live hand-to-mouth.
Nickel also hit stops, sliding as low as $7,100 before support buoyed the market.
Last trade was $40 softer at $7,210.
Supply fears still underpin the market, as a strike at Inco's Sudbury operations drags on and Russia's Norilsk Nickel tries to solve its energy problems.
"Prices need to get back above $7,400 before the market looks good again," Adams said.
Chartists placed next major support at the June 2 low of $6910.
Zinc edged up to a fresh peak at one point, adding $2 to Monday's high to hit $1,379, but scale-up selling and profit taking capped the move.
The overall move was an extension of a sideways pattern near recent highs, with last business $5 weaker at $1,368.
Tin dipped, but put on the brakes before reaching the recent low of $5,510, touching a low of $5,525.
This market also managed a bounce, ending the day $10 firmer at $5,570.
Alloy closed weaker at $1,465, down from $1,475/80 on Monday.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
